open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry sequence number
open_points.text: A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number
open_points.question: Does “the backup's last number” mean the persisted high-water mark of every sequence number ever written as of that backup, or the greatest audit entry still present in the backup after older entries have been erased?
options: Restore the persisted high-water mark and mint the next entry as that mark plus one
Use the greatest surviving entry, or 0 if none survive
Record a separate starting number for each restored history
open_points.default_guess: Persist the high-water mark in every backup and mint the next entry as that mark plus one.

open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: never reused within that history ... A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number
open_points.question: When a restored history later reuses sequence numbers that the lost history had written after the backup, is an AuditEntry identified only by its sequence number within the current store history, or must a store-history identity also distinguish entries across histories?
options: Sequence number scoped to one store history is the complete identity
AuditEntry identity is store-history identity plus sequence number
Sequence numbers must remain unique across restored histories using an external high-water mark
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence number as scoped to one store history, with no separately stored history identity.

open_points.subject: Model M10 — MigrationClosure persistence
open_points.text: absent, then present for the rest of the store's history ... a store restored after a loss from a backup made before the import begins a history without it ... Durable, at most one per instance
open_points.question: Is MigrationClosure cardinality at most one per store history, allowing the same production instance to acquire a new closure after restore and re-import, or at most one across the entire lifetime of the instance?
options: At most one per store history
At most one across the instance's lifetime
A restore creates a new instance for this model's identity and cardinality
open_points.default_guess: At most one per store history; a restore from before the import permits a new closure after re-import.
